title: The Layers Still Falling Where Soil Is Becoming

features.name: the-house-becoming
features.desc-on-touch: A small weatherboard cottage is half-buried, half-emerging. The soil cannot decide whether to claim it or release it. Both are happening at once.

features.name: the-shed-that-remembers-falling
features.desc-on-touch: This shed is not falling. It has fallen, and the earth is still learning what shape to give it. The roof timber reads like a date.

features.name: the-settling-narration
features.desc-on-touch: The layers fall, carrying stories down. You can read the ages by the objects caught between them: a button, a coin, a slip of paper that used to matter.

features.name: the-soil-s-active-patience
features.desc-on-touch: The earth here is not resting. It is becoming. Each layer of soil is learning what it means to carry, to hold, to eventually refuse.

features.name: the-root-that-reads-what-fell
features.desc-on-touch: A root has wound through the layers, through the narrative that is settling. It reads the past by growing through it, comparing each age it passes.

inscription: here the narrative is not yet still; the layers continue to fall, and the soil continues to learn what to do with all this weight and time

file.name: Homestead_Site_Profile_Layers_Early20thCent.txt
file.note: Soil core from beneath a razed house. Each layer marked with age and artifact. Corruption: the objects in the lower layers appear before they were made. The soil is remembering things forward.

reverie.title: REVERIE — standing where the shed still stands
narr: The old shed is still here, timber blackening into the earth.
You stand beside her in the failing light, watching it become
soil. 'It'll be here a long time,' she says, 'before the earth
finishes with it.' You see it both ways at once: the building
it was, and the layers it's becoming. She takes your hand.
'Everything falls. The ground just remembers slowly.'

upward where the objects emerge and remember their names
